title: Ask the author: a question's round trip
summary: Follow one reviewer question from tarot to the implementing agent and back: lookup, create, compose, deliver (live / resume / gone), capture, record.
author: agent:claude (review tour)

steps.title: 1 · The review tool finds the author
steps.note: Entry point: tarot resolves the PR it is reviewing to the implementing task -- GET /tasks/lookup by url, or repo_id+branch. Exactly one selector; returns the full task so the reviewer's side sees the same shape as GET /tasks/{id}.

steps.title: 2 · One outstanding ask per task
steps.note: POST /tasks/{id}/ask creates the Ask. AskInProgress (409) if one is already outstanding, AskGone (410) if the agent's session is unrecoverable. Creating sets pending_ask_id on the task -- the delivery daemon's self-gating signal.

steps.title: 3 · An ask's life in four states
steps.note: PENDING (created, undelivered) -> DELIVERED (injected into the agent) -> ANSWERED (reply recorded). GONE is the honest dead end: the claude session no longer exists, surfaced to tarot as a 410 so it can offer a surrogate instead.

steps.title: 4 · The letter, with a tracking number
steps.note: The delivered message: the ask marker first ([[...:ask_id]] -- the Stop hook anchors on it), then framing. Terminal tasks get the strict guardrail (answer only, touch nothing); in-flight tasks get a lighter note since a reviewer's question may legitimately prompt a fix.

steps.title: 5 · Delivery triage on the host daemon
steps.note: Each daemon pass calls deliver() per task; pending_ask_id makes it a no-op otherwise. Ownership guard first (sessions/volumes are host-local). Then: live tmux session -> inject; config volume gone -> mark GONE; otherwise resume the parked agent (step 6). Delivered is marked only after one of these succeeds.

steps.title: 6 · Waking a finished author
steps.note: The deliberate difference from spawn_one: TERMINAL tasks are allowed -- asking a COMPLETE task's author is first-class. The config volume holds the claude session, so --continue resumes it with the ask as the prompt. Claim is compare-and-set; losing the race leaves the ask pending for the winning host.

steps.title: 7 · Reading the reply off the transcript
steps.note: The Stop hook fires when the agent finishes its turn. extract_answer finds the LAST user message carrying the marker and joins the assistant text up to the next user turn. Pure and fixture-testable; returns None until the reply exists -- recording is best-effort by design.

steps.title: 8 · The answer lands
steps.note: The hook posts the reply; the ask flips to ANSWERED and pending_ask_id clears. tarot's PanopticonBackend has been polling GET .../asks/{id} -- the answer renders in the reviewer's A panel labeled author-claimed. Round trip complete.
